sections.title: Shrub and leaves
sections.text: Rhododendron catawbiense is an evergreen, rounded shrub native to the southern Appalachian Mountains. It commonly grows about 1.8–3 m tall and 2.4–3 m wide, with leathery leaves crowded near branch tips.

sections.title: Flowers and capsules
sections.text: Showy lavender to purple, five-lobed flowers form terminal clusters; the corolla is about 1.5–3.7 cm long. A dry, five-valved capsule follows flowering.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: This species contains grayanotoxins and is listed as poisonous; do not eat any part. The plate's evergreen shrub, purple flower clusters and capsules agree with the species.
